messages:
maya: heads-up bringing up cyclone-17b (int4) canary. microbatch=1 + kv-prefetch enabled. stress tests hit OOMs with very long contexts (~30k tokens).

drew: which quant backend? block-quant or per-layer?

maya: block-quant with hybrid fallback. defaults we used: max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch.window_tokens=512.

liam: fragmentation typically surfaces with long generation tails. can you repro if kv_prefetch=false?

maya: disabling prefetch prevents the OOM at 1024 but throughput drops ~8%. also tried max_new_tokens=256 with prefetch=true and that passes.

ana: saw similar on certon. shrinking prefetch.window_tokens helps. baseline suggestion: prefetch.window_tokens=128 and batching.window_ms=6.

maya: applied prefetch.window_tokens=128 + kept max_new_tokens=1024 -> stable on canary for 30m. heap spikes reduced. throughput ~3% lower, acceptable.

drew: try adding slot compaction + soft eviction for long-lived KV. config snippet I used:

"inference": { "batching": {"window_ms":6}, "kv": {"prefetch": {"window_tokens":128}, "slot_compaction":true, "soft_evict_threshold_pct":85}, "generation": {"max_new_tokens":1024} }

maya: tested locally with that config. canary stayed up, evictions visible but graceful.

ops-bot: canary rollout -> 3 nodes us-west-2. alerts enabled.

maya: proposed plan: 1) lower model default max_new_tokens to 512 to reduce tail risk; 2) set prefetch.window_tokens=128 in model profile; 3) enable slot_compaction + soft_evict on canary; 4) add smoke test that generates 20k tokens.

drew: I'll draft the PR for the model profile + smoke test in the eval harness.

liam: I'll run perf benches to quantify throughput regression and capture allocator histograms.

ana: note for release notes: surface the stability/perf trade-off.

maya: thanks all, will attach traces and heap graphs in the PR.
